is_anopheles.evidence: Indoor trapping of An. gambiae s.s., An. arabiensis, and An. funestus s.s. was performed (Page 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: PCR and direct DNA sequencing were performed to identify point mutations at 1014 L (L1014S) in the field-collected mosquitoes (Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The allelic frequency of the point mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel (L1014S) in the collected mosquitoes was 98.4% (n = 96, Accession AB776705, AB776706) (Page 5).

african_field_population.evidence: Field collections of mosquitoes were conducted in Mfangano Island, Nyaroya Village, and Ungoe Village in western Kenya (Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: The study performed primary field collections and laboratory analysis of mosquito blood-feeding and resistance markers (Page 1-3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Mfangano Island, Nyaroya Village, and Ungoe Village in Mbita and Suba districts, western Kenya (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted from May 16 to June 1, 2011; October 4 to 31, 2011; February 21 to March 6, 2012; and July 11 to 18, 2012 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original field trap collections conducted specifically for this study in 2011-2012.

supplement.evidence: All required genotype frequency and sample size data are present in the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the preventive effect of permethrin-impregnated bed nets on blood feeding in pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.s., An. arabiensis, and An. funestus s.s. in western Kenya between 2011 and 2012. Sequencing of the voltage-gated sodium channel in field-collected An. gambiae s.s. revealed a Vgsc L1014S (L995S) allele frequency of 98.4% (n = 96).
